standard_text: Morphology of different parts of flowering plants: root, stem, leaf, inflorescence, flower, fruit and seed. Description of family Solanaceae.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 5 Morphology of Flowering Plants: roots, stems and leaves and their modifications, inflorescence, flowers, aestivation, placentation, fruits, seeds and families. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Root, stem and leaf can all be modified.
key_sub: Aestivation is how petals are arranged in a bud; placentation is how ovules are arranged in an ovary.
body_html:
How to think about it

Dicots usually have tap roots and reticulate venation; monocots have fibrous roots and parallel venation. Roots, stems and leaves are modified for storage, support, climbing and protection: carrots are roots, potatoes are stems and pea tendrils are leaves.

A flower is described by its symmetry, ovary position (hypogynous, perigynous, epigynous), aestivation (valvate, twisted, imbricate, vexillary) and placentation. Families such as Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae are known by their floral features.

Example

Potato is a modified?

it has eyes (nodes)

Answer: stem

Example

Placentation in pea?

one-chambered ovary

Answer: marginal

Common mistakes

  • Calling potato a root.
  • Mixing up twisted and imbricate aestivation.
  • Calling a coconut's water the fruit wall.

faq.a: It has nodes (eyes) with buds that grow into new shoots.
